title: Philliberto: The Villain Who Keeps Coming Back
body: Every league needs a bad guy, and the Buckaroo Football League found its man on day one. Alan, known around the league as Philly, Phillibert, or Philliberto, has run Team Pillbert since the league was founded in 2023. Four seasons in, he has no Buckaroo Bowl titles but also zero last-place finishes. That is exactly the kind of quiet consistency that makes a villain dangerous.

His debut was nearly a coronation. Team Pillbert went 9-5, scored 1,499.3 points, grabbed the 2 seed, and finished second of six. That means Philly was one game away from lifting Buckaroo Bowl I, only for Kaushal's Habibsters to take the crown. Along the way he posted his career-best week, a 156.2-point demolition of Sonny in Week 3. The 2024 season was bumpier: a 6-8 record still sneaked him in as the 4 seed, and he climbed to third. That year also produced his low point, a 64.1-point dud against, naturally, Kaushal.

Then came 2025, the strangest season on his ledger. Team Pillbert piled up a career-high 1,762.9 points but somehow went 5-11, the kind of record that suggests the schedule had a personal grudge. He still squeezed in as the 6 seed and finished fourth of six. The low comedy of the year came in Week 9, when he lost 94.76 to 92.02 to Ramon's Remains, a team whose manager had literally been kicked out of the league. Brucie gets that win with an asterisk, and Phillibert gets a story he will never live down.

The head-to-head ledger shows who Alan likes to torment. He owns Randy at 8-5, leads Mekhi 6-4, and edges Ramon 6-5 in a battle between the league's two favorite heels. Sonny has him narrowly at 6-5. Then there is Kaushal, Philly's personal kryptonite, who leads the series 2-7. Against the newcomers he is 1-0 against Jordan and 0-1 against Zoe, so the rookie has already gotten one over on the bad guy.

The 2026 version of Philliberto looks like a man who got tired of waiting. After making zero trades in his first two seasons and just one in 2025, he has already pulled the trigger on four deals this year. He keeps grinding the waiver wire too, with 16 pickups to go with 11, 21, and 25 in past seasons. The results are showing: Team Pillbert sits at 5-2 with 817.8 points and a 17% shot at the title. The villain is back in the hunt, and the rest of the league should be nervous.
